On physical examination, the patient appears thin and mildly tachypneic at rest.
Lung examination reveals decreased breath sounds and prolonged expiration without wheezing or rales.
There is mild hyperresonance to percussion bilaterally, and his chest appears slightly increased in anteroposterior diameter.
No digital clubbing is observed.
Cardiovascular and abdominal exams are normal, and there is no lower extremity edema.
A chest x-ray reveals bilateral hyperlucency of the lung fields and several large bullae in the lower lobes.
His workup is pending, but based on the presentation and imaging findings, his clinician explains that certain measurable parameters of lung physiology are already likely to be abnormal.
The patient is referred for further testing and genetic counseling.
He is worried about his long-term prognosis and asks how this condition affects gas exchange.
